examples.en: The bullet went through the wall.
This road runs right through the middle of the city.

examples.ko: 터널이 산을 관통하는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years for the tunnel to cut through the mountain.
Be careful that the nail does not go through the board.
The Han River flows through Seoul.
This railway is planned to run across the country.

explain: 무언가가 한쪽에서 반대쪽까지 뚫고 지나갈 때 써요. 길, 강, 터널이 도시나 산을 가로지를 때도 '관통하다'라고 해요. '서울을 관통하다'처럼 목적어에 '을/를'을 붙여요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 물건이 아니라 책, 글, 시대 전체에 계속 흐르는 생각이나 주제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not for physical objects but for an idea or theme that runs through a whole book, text or era.

explain_en: Use it when something pierces or passes through from one side to the other. Roads, rivers and tunnels that cut across a city or mountain also 관통하다. The object takes '을/를', as in '서울을 관통하다'.

examples.ko: 그 집은 땅뙈기 하나 없이 시작했어요.
examples.en: That family started out without even a small patch of land.
I planted lettuce and peppers on a small patch of land.
If I had even a small patch of land, I would farm it.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 마지막 땅뙈기까지 팔아서 아들을 가르쳤어요.
examples.en: Grandfather sold even his last bit of land to educate his son.
It is hard to make a living from a small plot like this.

examples.ko: 손바닥만 한 땅뙈기를 가지고 형제가 다퉜어요.
examples.en: The brothers quarreled over a tiny plot of land.

explain: 작은 땅을 조금 낮추거나 하찮게 말하는 느낌이에요. '땅뙈기 하나 없다'처럼 없거나 적다는 문맥에서 많이 나와요. 넓은 땅에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 땅뙈기 하나 없이 도시로 올라왔어요.
phrases.en: He came up to the city without owning even a patch of land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하나' 뒤에 '없다'가 오면 아주 가진 것이 없다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '하나' followed by '없다', it means having nothing at all.

phrases.example: 작은 땅뙈기라도 있으면 채소를 키우고 싶어요.
phrases.en: If I had even a tiny patch of land, I'd like to grow vegetables.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes how small the land is.

phrases.example: 우리 집은 땅뙈기도 없어서 농사를 못 지어요.
phrases.en: We don't even have a plot of land, so we can't farm.
phrases.en_equiv: to not even have a patch of land

explain_en: It refers to a small piece of land in a slightly belittling way. It often appears in negative contexts like '땅뙈기 하나 없다' (not to have even a bit of land). It is not used for large areas of land.

examples.ko: 책꽂이에는 교과서 외에도 소설책과 시집이 빽빽이 꽂혀 있어요.
examples.en: Besides textbooks, novels and poetry books are packed tightly on the bookshelf.

examples.ko: 버스 안에 사람들이 빽빽이 서 있어요.
examples.en: People are standing packed tightly inside the bus.
Trees stand densely packed in the forest.
I filled my notebook with tightly written notes.
Cars are parked bumper to bumper in the lot.

examples.ko: 좁은 사무실에 책상이 빽빽이 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Desks are crammed tightly into the small office.

explain: 사이에 빈틈이 거의 없이 촘촘한 모습이에요. '빼곡히'와 아주 비슷하게 쓰고, 반대로 듬성듬성한 모습은 '듬성듬성'이라고 해요. 형용사 '빽빽하다'의 부사형이라서 '빽빽하게'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Photos are packed all over the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning and interchangeable.

phrases.nuance_ko: '빽빽이'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'ppaekppaegi' and more common in speech.

phrases.example: 나무가 빽빽한 숲이라 햇빛이 잘 안 들어요.
phrases.en: It's a dense forest, so little sunlight comes in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '빽빽하다'의 활용으로, 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form 'ppaekppaekhada' modifying the noun after it.

explain_en: It describes things placed very close together with almost no gaps. It is used much like '빼곡히', and the opposite is '듬성듬성' (sparsely). It is the adverb form of the adjective '빽빽하다', so '빽빽하게' also works.

examples.en: The subway is always packed during rush hour.

examples.ko: 주말이라 식당이 초만원이라서 한 시간 기다렸어요.
examples.en: It was the weekend and the restaurant was jam-packed, so I waited an hour.
Because of the rain, the bus was totally full.
I heard every hotel is completely full because of the festival.
I barely managed to get on the packed elevator.
The concert hall was filled to capacity, so I watched standing.

explain: '만원'보다 훨씬 꽉 찬 느낌으로, 사람이 넘치는 지하철, 식당, 공연장에 많이 써요. '초만원이다', '초만원을 이루다'로 쓰고, 반대로 사람이 없으면 '텅 비다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I stood for a long time on the jam-packed subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 아주 꽉 찬 장소나 탈것을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a jam-packed place or vehicle.

phrases.en: The concert hall was packed to the brim with fans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많이 모여 자리가 하나도 없는 모습을 글에서 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in writing to describe a place with no seats left because of the crowd.
phrases.en_equiv: to be packed to the brim

phrases.en: The bus was full, so I couldn't get on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '초만원'보다 약하고 일상에서 더 흔하게 '가득 찼다'는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Weaker than 초만원 and more common in daily speech for 'full'.

explain_en: It feels much fuller than '만원' and is often used for overflowing subways, restaurants, and venues. You say '초만원이다' or '초만원을 이루다', and the opposite situation is '텅 비다' (to be empty).

examples.en: The old warehouse was transformed into a cafe.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 관광 도시로 탈바꿈하고 있어요.
examples.en: This area is transforming into a tourist city.

examples.ko: 머리와 옷을 바꾸니까 완전히 탈바꿈한 것 같아요.
examples.en: With the new hair and clothes, you look completely transformed.

examples.ko: 가게가 새롭게 탈바꿈하려면 돈이 꽤 들어요.
examples.en: It costs quite a lot for a shop to get a fresh makeover.

examples.ko: 오래된 시장이 젊은 사람들이 찾는 곳으로 탈바꿈해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the old market turned into a place young people visit.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 온라인 중심으로 탈바꿈할 거예요.
examples.en: That company will transform to focus on online business.

explain: '~이/가 ~(으)로 탈바꿈하다' 형태로 자주 써요. '변하다'보다 눈에 띄게 확 바뀐다는 느낌이고, 좋은 쪽으로 새롭게 바뀔 때 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '변신하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: The old park has been newly transformed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 쪽으로 새로워졌다는 느낌을 더할 때 '새롭게'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 새롭게 to give a feeling of changing for the better.

phrases.example: 그들은 낡은 건물을 예쁜 카페로 탈바꿈시켰어요.
phrases.en: They transformed the old building into a pretty cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어가 다른 것을 바꿀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when the subject changes something else.

phrases.en: A caterpillar transforms into a butterfly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탈바꿈하다와 비슷하게 모습이 확 바뀔 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 탈바꿈하다 for a sudden change of appearance.

explain_en: It is often used in the pattern '~이/가 ~(으)로 탈바꿈하다'. Compared with '변하다' (to change), it feels like a striking, sudden change, and is often used for changing into something new and better. '변신하다' is a similar word.
